findings.text: The cutover's identity proof covers two cells and two points (72 entries, 0 byte differences), not done_when clause (2), which requires the built jet rows to match at every node of the 282-cell arm and at a fixed 64-node subset of the 2,132-node arm; a 4-value fixture is filed against a 2,132-node build.

The suite section records two arms over tests/test_fixed_points.py plus the new budget test and nothing about done_when clause (3), the 500-cell census test the done_when itself calls the binding measure: no run, no 900 s timeout result and no --mem=64G receipt is recorded, so the record presents a partial measure as the node's evidence.

The docstring claims 'a reduced cell count measures the same graph the production rows compile', but the node's own receipt lowered-size-summary.json measures production_point_batch at 8 cells at 8,408,375 StableHLO bytes against this fixture's 5,442,157, so the 6,000,000 ceiling sits below the production graph it is said to stand for and the guard is calibrated on a different program instance.

The landed cutover deleted the _source_jets definition this prototype parses out of read_route/jets.py to key its cache, so that check now fails; the worker recorded it under outside_scope rather than editing it, but the node's change is what makes the failure reachable and no test covers the prototype.

The negative control actually run (unrolling the moment evaluation to 27,479,507 bytes) falsifies the graph-budget test, not the control the node declared ('restoring the base point program in fixed_points.py makes the 60 s compile bound at the 282-cell arm fail'); the declared control is neither run nor shown unattainable, so the guard that was proved and the guard that was declared are different guards.
